issue.title: mavlink_direct: Message filtering not working in subscribe_message (v3.10.1)
issue.body:
## Bug Description
The `mavlink_direct` plugin's `subscribe_message` method does not properly filter messages when a specific `message_name` is provided. Instead of receiving only the requested message type, subscribers receive ALL message types.

## Expected Behavior
When subscribing with a specific message name (e.g., `message_name="HEARTBEAT"`), the subscriber should only receive messages of that type.

## Actual Behavior
Subscribers receive ALL message types regardless of the filter specified. The `message_name` parameter is completely ignored.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start MAVSDK server v3.10.1
2. Connect via gRPC and use the mavlink_direct service
3. Call `SubscribeMessage` with `message_name="HEARTBEAT"`
4. Observe that you receive all message types (ATTITUDE, TIMESYNC, GPS_RAW_INT, etc.)

## Test Results
Testing with a Python gRPC client shows:
- **No filter (empty string)**: Correctly receives all 34 message types
- **Filter "HEARTBEAT"**: Incorrectly receives all 34 message types (should only receive HEARTBEAT)
- **Filter "TIMESYNC"**: Incorrectly receives all 34 message types (should only receive TIMESYNC)
- **Filter "ATTITUDE"**: Incorrectly receives all 34 message types (should only receive ATTITUDE)

## Root Cause Analysis
Looking at the code in `mavlink_direct_impl.cpp`:
- The `subscribe_message` method stores the `message_name` filter
- It registers with `SystemImpl::register_libmav_message_handler`
- However, when messages arrive, they're forwarded to ALL subscribers regardless of their individual filters
- The stored `message_name` is never actually used to filter messages before invoking callbacks

## Environment
- MAVSDK version: v3.10.1
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Connection: gRPC on port 50051
- Test vehicle: PX4 SITL

## Workaround
Until fixed, users must manually filter messages in their client code:
```python
# Subscribe to all messages (empty filter)
request = mavlink_direct_pb2.SubscribeMessageRequest(message_name="")
responses = stub.SubscribeMessage(request)

for response in responses:
    if response.HasField('message'):
        msg = response.message
        # Manual filtering
        if msg.message_name == "HEARTBEAT":
            # Process only HEARTBEAT messages
            process_message(msg)
```

## Impact
This bug makes the filtering feature completely non-functional, forcing all clients to receive and process all messages, which can significantly impact performance in high-frequency telemetry scenarios.

comments.body: Thanks for the report. That doesn't sound right indeed!

Hm, I can't reproduce this.

So, the subscription happens here:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/872f17c566b3099520c4de7336977fde6f6ce84f/src/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_direct/mavlink_direct_impl.cpp#L148-L149

which goes here:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/872f17c566b3099520c4de7336977fde6f6ce84f/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L165-L174

And the filtering happens here:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/872f17c566b3099520c4de7336977fde6f6ce84f/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L140-L145

And last I checked it was correct in my Python example. What am I missing?

Hi @julianoes,

Thanks for looking into this. I tested with v3.10.1 and can still reproduce the issue. I think I found where the problem might be.

The filtering you pointed to in `system_impl.cpp` works correctly:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/872f17c566b3099520c4de7336977fde6f6ce84f/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L140-L145

However, the issue seems to be in how `mavlink_direct_impl.cpp` handles the callbacks after filtering. When subscribing, it registers this handler:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/872f17c566b3099520c4de7336977fde6f6ce84f/src/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_direct/mavlink_direct_impl.cpp#L148-L166

The callback at line 150-163 receives the correctly filtered message, but then at line 161 it calls:

```cpp
_message_subscriptions.queue(direct_message, [this](const auto& func) {
    _system_impl->call_user_callback(func);
});
```

This `_message_subscriptions.queue()` broadcasts the message to ALL subscribers of MavlinkDirect, not just the ones who subscribed to that specific message type. The `_message_subscriptions` is a single `CallbackList` that doesn't differentiate between what each subscriber originally requested.

So the flow is:
1. User A subscribes to "HEARTBEAT"  
2. User B subscribes to "GPS_RAW_INT"
3. Both callbacks get registered in the same `_message_subscriptions` list
4. When a HEARTBEAT arrives, it passes the filter and triggers User A's handler
5. But that handler broadcasts the HEARTBEAT to both User A and User B

Here's my test output with gRPC client against v3.10.1:
```
Subscribing to: "HEARTBEAT"
Received: ATTITUDE
Received: GLOBAL_POSITION_INT  
Received: HIGHRES_IMU
...
```

I could provide a minimal reproduction script if that would help. Let me know if I'm misunderstanding how the CallbackList is supposed to work!
As Claude would say "[You're absolutely right!](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/3382)" Thanks for looking into it. Fix coming.
@ayatim let me know if this is fixed for you.

issue.title: mavlink_direct: fix message filtering

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
The message filtering was not correct with 2 or more subscriptions as they would conflict with each other. This should now be fixed with each subscription keeping track of what to filter out.

While doing so we switched to the new and nicer Handle/Subscription API in SystemImpl rather than the ugly void* cookie thing.

Fixes #2648.
